schoolReviews.review: My daughter was there for two years, the academic requirement is good, they are bilingual and they attend to both languages equally, the activities at the school are adorable... The social skills of some teachers and field staff need to be worked on. But academically it seemed good to me compared to other schools in Austin that have very good scores which they do not deserve, such as Steiner Ranch and Summitt.

Even though the communication and organization for some events could have been better, I want to say I was extremely pleased with this school during the 2014-2015 school year. Ms. Karkos was an amazing teacher. She takes the time to know each student and not only works hard to develop their brains, but also works very hard to show them how to be wonderful members of a community. The LEAD program was amazing. Lots of ppl on staff who care deeply for the children. Thank you Smith Elementary!
THEY CARE and they do A lot for ALL the kids. At times they have exceeded my expectations. LOVE Smith

Everything the Post from April 14, 2013 says PLUS I am OUTRAGED to find that they issue detention to Pre-K age children for tardies. How is punishing a 3 year old by giving their parent's more free time to do whatever they want for an extra few hours constructive? Anyone?

First off the office staff is not very welcoming. The school does not make you feel welcome at all. I understand that there are security measures to follow, but not being able to walk your child to class is ridiculous, and the way they have the pick up set up is terrible. Basically all the parents wait in a small area at the front and wait for the childs name to be called to go home. This can take a while, because sometimes the teachers dont have the children in the lunch room when they are calling names already. Also the lunch monitors are extremely rude and yelll constantly at the children. There are better ways to communicate with them. The menu itself is terrible, but that is a different topic. Overall we have been happy with the teacher and academics, but not feeling welcome is sad. AISD is not the best, but at least when we volunteered or visited the schools, the staff was always friendly and encouraging. Also they are always late to send out notifications. Everything seems to be last minute for them, such as events and they do not seem organized at all.

Friendly, On top of things as best as possible, organized and has been very helpful for my child who struggles a bit. I feel that my child is safe. Is the school perfect, no. But I can tell you from switching my child from another school in Del Valle this school is WAY better then the others. REMEMBER we are in TX. GOP controls, so there is a lot of lacking of good resources to help our teachers and other staff members; especially on East side.

Within the first two weeks of kinder they lost track of our child. A teacher instructed our daughter to ride the bus even though she was given a sign to wear around her neck that says parent pick up. They only allow parents three days to help walk their child to class. Most kids where crying the first week as parent were made to stand and watch their child being ushered by some school rep they've barely been introduced to. Horrible communication about upcoming events, they send notices out the day before or the day of parent involved school events. They performed, without any notice, an emergency drill in reaction to sandy hook, our daughter said she was scared that somebody had hurt us and she was confused on what was happening.

schoolReviews.review: They had my 6th grader out side for 3 hr with no water no nothing no air no snacks my child called me in tears
Ojeda's teachers are motivated and engaged to "do whatever it takes" to help their students succeed.

My daughter attended this school for one year (7th grade) and that was enough, complete lack of teacher and parent involvement, thus poor student academics. I noticed a drop in my daughters grades and took the initiative to call teachers and make conferences, one teacher took one complete month to return call, the other one was two months, was absurd but only way to get a conference call was by " throwing a fit in front office" i had tried email, phone calls left msg with asst principal and was of no use. new principal has strong leadership skills but long way to go among teachers and staff. Academics is not taken seriously at this school, seems like it is just a daycare for teens. School website is not up to date. Librarian is one of the few excellent teachers at this school. I currently enrolled my teen at Harmony school of excellence, so far she has had more homework than at this school (which i appreciate) will let you know about other school within a year. overall i really feel ojeda was a waste of my time and nothing productive was learned besides social interaction, look elsewhere if you want a school that will prepare for college, perfect if u want daycare for child

I am a community member, educator, and school leader in a local district, and I had the privilege of spending a day at Ojeda Middle School. I was blown away by the quality of education students at Ojeda were receiving. The new principal, Mr. Williams, is a strong leader who feels his job is to hire great people and remove the barriers to them doing their job well. He has set up clear behavioral, academic, and social expectations, and systems to support all members of the learning community to reach them. His unwavering belief in the capabilities of his colleagues and students to overcome every obstacle are refreshing. I believe that Ojeda Middle will soon be one of the most celebrated middle schools in Central Texas as long as he is there enabling everyone to reach their potential. Given the opportunity, I would send my own children to Ojeda without hesitation.
